assertion_results.description: At least one eval record has a grade assigned
At least one eval record carries an ISO last_graded timestamp (the skill's actual deliverable is in-place grading updates to eval records, not a standalone output file)
At least one graded eval record has substantive grader_notes (>20 chars) explaining the grade rationale

grading.grader_notes: rigby-eval-grade signal record. 3/3 assertions passed but vacuously — they check global state ('at least one eval record has a grade assigned' is true historically), not this run's deliverable. Zero grades were actually written today before this sweep, so the run produced no verifiable grading output. Two possibilities: its filter legitimately selected only excludable records (unknown/phantom dominate the recent tail), or it silently no-op'd. Either way the assertions as designed cannot distinguish a productive grading run from an empty one — that is an assertion-design defect worth fixing (assert grades_written>0 for the selected set, or record the skip rationale).
